name: GET /api/leadflow/sla/config - the business calendar, the 30-minute policy and the clock rules
description:
The SLA configuration behind SOP §04, the customer number-one non-negotiable.

A NAMED IANA ZONE, NEVER A FIXED OFFSET (3e3ba115-8015-447d-afa1-4aadc2fe1e3a#AC1). "UTC-6" is correct for America/Chicago for about four months of the year and an hour wrong for the rest, so a fixed offset produces deadlines that are silently 60 minutes out either side of every DST transition - in March it makes a met SLA look breached, and in November it hides a real one. Every wall-clock calculation goes through Intl.DateTimeFormat with the zone NAME, so the platform tz database supplies the transition rules rather than this codebase assuming them. The response carries timezone_kind:"iana_named_zone" and fixed_offset:null so a consumer can see which it is getting.

THE 4:59PM RULE IS SERVED AS A WORKED EXAMPLE, not just as prose (3e3ba115-8015-447d-afa1-4aadc2fe1e3a#AC2). Pass ?at= and the response computes that instant through the SAME function that computes real deadlines: a 16:59 America/Chicago arrival returns due 17:29 with requires_late_coverage true. Both alternative implementations lie - clamping the deadline to 17:00 gives the customer 1 minute instead of 30, and deferring to the next morning quietly converts a 30-minute promise into a 16-hour one. Either way the CRM would hide an impossible SLA behind a green number, which SOP §04 names as the failure to avoid. Verified live: at=2026-08-11T21:59:00Z returned local 16:59, due 22:29Z, requires_late_coverage true.

THE CLOCK SURVIVES EVERY HANDOVER (3e3ba115-8015-447d-afa1-4aadc2fe1e3a#AC3), and that is enforced rather than documented: migration 024 installs a BEFORE UPDATE trigger on leads that RAISES if source_timestamp changes, so merge, reassignment and backup takeover cannot reset it from any code path. Proven end to end under task b736b718 - three handovers plus an accept moved assigned_at each time while source_timestamp and sla_due_at held.

HOLIDAYS ARE A LIST, NOT A RULE (3e3ba115-8015-447d-afa1-4aadc2fe1e3a#AC4). The observed date of a holiday falling at a weekend is a business decision rather than a calculation, and half of them move every year, so RevOps maintains the list and the code does not guess.

Open to any authenticated caller: this is configuration a rep needs in order to understand their own deadline, and gating it would leave people guessing at the rule they are measured against. QA: depends on register and login.

testCases.name: The calendar reports a named zone rather than a fixed offset
A 16:59 Central arrival is due at 17:29 and needs late coverage
A weekend arrival defers to the next business morning
NEGATIVE: an unparseable probe instant is refused rather than silently treated as now
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.message: at must be a valid ISO timestamp
errorCases.when: the probe instant cannot be parsed. Silently substituting now would answer a question about a different moment from the one asked, and the caller would read the deadline as applying to their instant.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
